body:
I happened to be in the process of benchmarking this, so I might as well share the numbers. With the following (primitive) benchmark...
[Click to expand/collapse]

```gdscript extends Node2D const PLACEHOLDERS: Array[String] = ["{scale}", "{skew}", "{visible}", "{position}", "{rotation}", "{top_level}", "{z_index}", "{show_behind_parent}"] const RUNS := 10 func _ready() -> void: for str_len in [10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000]: for placeholder_count in [0, 1, 2, 4, 8]: var placeholders := "".join(PLACEHOLDERS.slice(0, placeholder_count)) if placeholders.length() > str_len: break var test_string := " ".repeat(str_len - placeholders.length()) + placeholders test_string.format(self) var ticks_start := Time.get_ticks_usec() for i in RUNS: test_string.format(self) var average = (Time.get_ticks_usec() - ticks_start) / float(RUNS) print("String of length %d with %d placeholders averaged %.2f µs" % [str_len, placeholder_count, average]) ```

... µs (+6.9%) String of length 1000000 with 8 placeholders averaged 83067.50 µs (+14.0%) ``` So I guess that largely matches intuition. Shorter strings are mostly faster because `contains` is cheaper than a property read, and longer strings are slower because `contains` starts taking time, which is then multiplied by the number of placeholders. Still though, I don't think the performance hit is that bad, but if someone is using `String.format` as some kind of template engine then they'll likely take a hit.

Given `contains()` is really just a `find() != -1` wrapper, could we feasibly use `find()` directly? `replace` doesn't appear to have a starting offset parameter, so that might not be an option at this time…

> `replace` doesn't appear to have a starting offset parameter, so that might not be an option at this time…

Having `String::format` use `_replace_common` directly and just add an `int p_from = 0` there that initializes the `search_from` variable we already have is easy enough, although it requires forward-declaring (or moving) `_replace_common`.

Adding a `from` parameter to the actual `replace` methods and their bound equivalents turns into a bigger change that I would assume warrants its own PR (and proposal?) so I'd prefer not to.

Here are the benchmark results of the `_replace_common` approach:

That looks a bit better obviously. The removal of the fixed cost from needlessly fetching unrelated properties presumably just blends into the margin of error towards the end there.

I've gone ahead and pushed this change, so you can see it for yourselves.

Were there any unresolved issues pending with this, or are we all fine with the `_replace_common` approach?

I guess one last unresolved bikeshed would be whether we want to forward-declare `_replace_common`, like I have now, or we just move it up (and presumably wreck blame history) to live above `String::format` instead.
